OFFICE OF THE COMPTROLLER OF THE CURRENCY
Washington, D.C. 20219

MATTER REQUIRING ATTENTION (MRA)
Confidential Supervisory Information — Do Not Disclose

Bank: First Heritage Commercial Bank, N.A. (Charter No. 24188)
Examination As-Of Date: December 31, 2025
Report Delivered: April 22, 2026
Examiner-in-Charge: Delphine R. Argueta, National Bank Examiner

MRA #1 — BANK SECRECY ACT / ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING PROGRAM DEFICIENCIES

1. FINDING
Examiners identified material weaknesses in the Bank's BSA/AML compliance program that constitute a violation of 12 C.F.R. § 21.21 and are inconsistent with safe and sound banking practices.

Specifically:
(a) The Bank's Customer Identification Program ("CIP") failed to obtain and verify required identifying information for 68 of the 400 new commercial account openings sampled during the examination period (17% exception rate; threshold: 5%).
(b) Suspicious Activity Reports ("SARs") were filed an average of 47 days after the initial detection of the underlying suspicious activity, exceeding the 30-day regulatory deadline established in 31 C.F.R. § 1020.320(b)(3).
(c) The Bank's automated transaction-monitoring system (Actimize Model AML-8) was last tuned in Q1 2023 and has not been recalibrated despite a 34% year-over-year increase in international wire volume.
(d) Enhanced Due Diligence ("EDD") files for 12 high-risk correspondent banking relationships were incomplete, missing beneficial ownership documentation required under 31 C.F.R. § 1010.230.
(e) The Bank's BSA Officer, Ms. Amara Delacroix, has responsibility for BSA compliance in addition to serving as Chief Compliance Officer and General Counsel, creating a lack of independent oversight.

2. ROOT CAUSE
The Bank's BSA/AML staffing is inadequate for the size and complexity of the Bank's operations. The BSA department has 4 full-time employees supporting an institution with $4.8 billion in assets and 42,000 commercial accounts. Peer benchmarks indicate 8-10 FTEs would be appropriate.

3. REQUIRED CORRECTIVE ACTION
The Board of Directors shall, within 90 days of the date of this MRA:
   (a) Retain a qualified independent third party to conduct a comprehensive BSA/AML risk assessment.
   (b) Hire a separate, dedicated BSA Officer with no other compliance responsibilities, reporting functionally to the Audit Committee.
   (c) Recalibrate the transaction-monitoring model with the assistance of a qualified model-validation firm.
   (d) Implement a remediation plan for the 68 CIP exceptions and provide a status report to the OCC Examiner-in-Charge within 60 days.
   (e) Provide quarterly progress reports to the OCC until this MRA is closed.

MRA #2 — CONCENTRATION RISK IN COMMERCIAL REAL ESTATE

Examiners noted that the Bank's non-owner-occupied commercial real estate ("CRE") concentration was 342% of Total Risk-Based Capital as of the examination date, exceeding the 300% supervisory threshold established in Interagency Guidance on CRE Concentrations (December 2006). Additionally, construction and land development loans represented 118% of Total Risk-Based Capital (supervisory threshold: 100%).

The Board shall adopt, within 60 days, a CRE Concentration Management Policy addressing (a) portfolio limits by property type, geography, and borrower, (b) enhanced stress-testing methodologies, and (c) a written plan for reducing concentrations to within supervisory thresholds within 24 months.

MRA #3 — INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY / CYBERSECURITY

The Bank's Business Continuity Plan has not been tested through a live tabletop exercise since May 2024. The most recent penetration test (conducted by KLM Cyber, September 2025) identified 14 high-severity vulnerabilities, of which 9 remained unremediated as of the examination date, exceeding the Bank's own 60-day remediation policy.

Required Corrective Action: (a) conduct a tabletop exercise no later than August 31, 2026; (b) remediate the 9 open high-severity vulnerabilities within 45 days.
